plan.summary: DIR-092 recon complete. FIRST, ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: the spec says DIR-091 'only implemented S1 (CubaMetricCardRow.jsx) and left S2-S6 unbuilt'. So the honest partial did its job: it produced this correctly-scoped follow-up. I intend to keep that discipline. SECOND, THE SCOPE HAS NOT ACTUALLY SHRUNK, AND YOU SHOULD KNOW THAT BEFORE I START: DIR-092 is titled a layout transformation but its spec enumerates SEVEN areas, which is the SAME seven I deferred - header, 4 metric cards, toolbar, resume cards, bottom analytics, right rail, sidebar promo. Splitting DIR-091 into DIR-092 re-issued the remainder as one directive rather than dividing it. Across this session the two six-part directives (DIR-088, DIR-090) both came back certified PARTIALS while the single-focus DIR-089 hit its target, and DIR-091 produced a certified partial at one of seven areas. If the goal is a COMPLETE delivery rather than a third partial, DIR-092 should be split again into DIR-092a and DIR-092b, and I recommend the seam below. If instead you want one pass, I will execute in value order and report exactly what landed. THIRD, THE ZERO-SYNTHETIC-DATA TENSION IS BACK AND IS SHARPER THIS TIME: the spec now names concrete content - documents called 'Master Resume', 'Software Engineer - Product', 'Data Analyst Resume' and 'UX Designer Resume', companies Google, Accenture and Infosys, and match figures 92, 86 and 78 percent - while still requiring zero synthetic data. Those names and numbers are illustrative of the reference screenshot, not facts about the account. My reading is unchanged from DIR-091: the LAYOUT is the specification and the VALUES must be real. So the status badges Master, Tailored and Draft will be DERIVED from real document state, ATS figures will come from the project's own scoring, job matches from the real matching module, and where a value genuinely does not exist the UI renders an explicit placeholder rather than inventing one. I will NOT hardcode 92 percent or a company called Infosys. If you want the screenshot's literal strings rendered as a visual mock, say so explicitly and I will scope it as a static mock instead - but I will not silently fabricate. FOURTH, MY RECON ESTABLISHED WHAT IS NEW VERSUS WHAT EXISTS, AND THIS DRIVES THE ORDER: the bottom three-column analytics DO NOT EXIST anywhere in src - a repo-wide sweep found Application Progress, Top Job Matches and Your Next Steps only in DashboardSettings and the marketing pricing page - and there is NO chart component in the codebase (only Form/progress-bar and marketing HomepageSteps). There is also NO Upgrade to Pro card in CubaAppShell. By contrast the header surface, the toolbar category pills, the resume card action row from DIR-086, and the rail's AiCareerBriefing plus Quick-Pitch ALL already exist. So areas 5 and 7 are greenfield builds and areas 1 through 4 and 6 are refinements. THE RECOMMENDED SEAM: DIR-092a would cover areas 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 - header, metric card polish, toolbar with Ctrl+K sort and Grid/List toggle, resume cards with badges and the dashed create card, the rail copilot, and the sidebar promo. That is all layout and wiring over data sources that ALREADY EXIST, so it is achievable completely in one pass. DIR-092b would cover area 5, the bottom analytics, which is the only genuinely new subsystem - it needs a real grouped bar chart built with no charting dependency, a real job-match list, and a next-steps checklist derived from real profile completeness, each needing its own data-lineage verification. I will execute in that order regardless: refinements first, analytics last, so that if budget runs out the delivered surface is coherent rather than half-built. INVARIANTS I WILL HOLD: sub-4s Vite build, 0 lint errors, frozen 55 CV templates at diff 0, XAMPP-only servers, zero synthetic data, no auth or API or DB or RBAC change, and tests/dir092-candidate-dashboard-reference-layout.test.mjs passing 100 percent. evidence.summary: DIR-092 HONEST PARTIAL  area 7 DELIVERED, areas 1 through 6 NOT DELIVERED, and I am saying so up front rather than letting a green suite imply a full match. WHAT LANDED: NEW src/components/cuba/CubaUpgradeCard.jsx, the sidebar Upgrade to Pro promo the reference anchors at the foot of the left sidebar  soft primary-to-info token gradient, crown badge, Upgrade to Pro title, the Unlock advanced AI tools benefit line and the Upgrade Now arrow CTA. It routes to a real plan route /dashboard/plans through the shell's existing onNavigate so it never reloads the document. ZERO FABRICATED DATA: a promo card has no per-user metric to fake, so it renders no counts, no percentages and no price, and AC3 asserts that in code. The one REAL input is the user's plan  when isPro is true the card reads You are on Pro and the CTA becomes Manage plan, so it never upsells an existing subscriber. The collapsed 72px rail degrades to an icon-only affordance that still carries a real aria-label and title, because an icon with no accessible name is an accessibility defect. Cuba tokens only, with AC5 asserting zero hardcoded hex and zero raw palette utilities. WIRED IN: CubaAppShell renders the card AFTER CubaNavGroups, which is flex-1, so the promo sits below the nav list without stealing its scroll  AC1 asserts that ordering rather than mere presence. I added an isPro prop defaulting to false so every existing caller keeps working and the shell never guesses a plan from a missing prop. I checked the available sets and switched to FaCrown from react-icons/fa, after which the build returned 0.
